title: Design and Verify an Incremental Dependency Scheduler
problem: Build systems change as their dependencies change. How can a scheduler keep those updates safe while still finding a valid build order? Design an algorithm that handles edge additions and removals, detects cycles, and returns a valid order when possible. Assume up to 100,000 vertices and 1,000,000 edges, with long sequences of updates and queries. Specify exact semantics for updates, including duplicate edges and nonexistent removals, data structures, pseudocode, correctness invariants and proofs, time and space complexity, and adversarial tests. Compare at least two approaches, including a straightforward recomputation baseline. Seek useful incremental performance without asserting an unproved bound. If worst-case efficient fully dynamic maintenance is not established, distinguish a correct implementable solution from a proposed optimization and give a discriminating benchmark.

strategies.title: Recompute baseline
strategies.approach: Implement a clear baseline that handles one update at a time: apply it, run a directed-cycle check, then produce a topological order if acyclic. Define duplicate-edge and missing-removal behavior first, and measure its cost over long update sequences.

strategies.title: Bounded dynamic-order experiment
strategies.approach: Choose one update rule and maintain a topological order while it remains valid. Prove the invariant for that rule, identify exactly when it fails, and compare the repair cost with the recomputation baseline on adversarial sequences. Do not claim a general worst-case bound from a benchmark.
